## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design cross-cloud, multi-environment Terraform architecture with centralized state, provider aliasing, drift handling, and automated gating. It also probes how to encode policy into CI and how to share data safely between clouds.

## Key Concepts
- Central remote backend with per-environment workspaces
- Terraform Cloud or similar as a single backend across clouds
- Provider aliases for multi-cloud deployments
- Cross-cloud data sharing via outputs and data sources
- Drift detection and safe remediation workflow
- CI gating: plan -out, review, then apply after approval

## Code Example
```hcl
terraform {
  backend "remote" {
    organization = "acme-org"
    workspaces {
      name = "platform-${var.env}"
    }
  }
}
```

```hcl
provider "aws" {
  region = var.aws_region
  alias  = "aws"
}

provider "google" {
  project = var.gcp_project
  region  = var.gcp_region
  alias   = "gcp"
}
```

- How would you enforce drift remediation when resources are mutated outside Terraform?
- How would you rotate credentials and protect state files in the central backend?

```rego
deny[msg] {
  input.kind == "plan"
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  region := r.change.after.region
  region notin ["us-east-1","us-west-2"]
  msg = sprintf("Region %v not allowed", [region])
}
```

```bash
# GitHub Actions (simplified)
name: Plan Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v1
      - name: Init Plan
        run: terraform init
      - name: Plan
        run: terraform plan -out=tfplan
      - name: OPA Gate
        run: |
          terraform show -json tfplan > plan.json
          opa eval --data policy.rego --input plan.json 'data.terraform.deny'
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This evaluates your ability to design a disaster recovery pattern across regions with strict isolation. It tests using remote state as a read-only data bridge, implementing per-environment backends, and creating CI gates to prevent accidental modifications to primary infrastructure.

## Key Concepts

- Cross-region isolation using Terraform remote state
- Provider aliasing for primary region access
- Per-environment backend configuration
- Read-only data consumption versus resource creation
- CI/CD gatekeeping for protection

## Code Example

```hcl
# Data bridge (DR repo)

terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket = "dr-terraform-state"
    key    = "network/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "us-west-2"
  }
}

provider "aws" {
  alias  = "primary"
  region = "us-east-1"
}

data "terraform_remote_state" "primary_vpc" {
  backend = "s3"
  config = {
    bucket = "primary-terraform-state"
    key    = "network/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "us-east-1"
  }
}

# Read-only consumption of primary resources
locals {
  primary_vpc_id = data.terraform_remote_state.primary_vpc.outputs.vpc_id
  primary_subnets = data.terraform_remote_state.primary_vpc.outputs.private_subnets
}

# DR resources only (no primary region resources)
resource "aws_vpc" "dr_vpc" {
  cidr_block = "10.20.0.0/16"
}
```

## CI/CD Gate Logic

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# CI gate to prevent primary region modifications

terraform plan -out=tfplan

# Check if any resources would be created/modified in primary region
if terraform show -json tfplan | jq -r '.planned_values.root_module.resources[] | select(.provider_name == "aws.primary") | .address' | grep -q .; then
  echo "ERROR: Plan contains changes in primary region (us-east-1)"
  echo "Changes found:"
  terraform show -json tfplan | jq -r '.planned_values.root_module.resources[] | select(.provider_name == "aws.primary") | "- \(.address)"'
  exit 1
fi

echo "✓ No primary region changes detected. Plan approved."
terraform apply tfplan
```

## Implementation Notes

- Primary repo exports VPC data via outputs
- DR repo only reads state data, never creates primary region resources
- Provider alias ensures correct region targeting
- CI gate parses JSON plan to detect any primary region changes
- State isolation through separate S3 backends per region

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts

- Terraform plan output as JSON for machine validation
- Remote state consumption of shared-network resources
- OPA/RegO-based policy to codify allowed vs disallowed changes
- Per-environment allowlists and central policy repository
- CI integration (GitHub Actions, CI gates, failure modes)

## Code Example

```rego
package terraform.shared_network

deny[reason] {
  some i
  change := input.resource_changes[i]
  change.change == "update"
  addr := change.address
  shared_resources := {"aws_vpc.shared","aws_subnet.shared","aws_security_group.shared"}
  addr in shared_resources
  not input.allowlist[addr]
  reason := sprintf("Disallowed change to %s", [addr])
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

```rego
package tf.guard

  input.plan_is_valid
```

questions.explanation:
## Terraform EC2 Instance with Security Group

### Core Resources
- `aws_instance`: Creates the EC2 virtual machine
- `aws_security_group`: Defines firewall rules for network access

### Implementation Example
```hcl
resource "aws_security_group" "web" {
  name        = "web-sg"
  description = "Allow HTTP traffic"

  ingress {
    from_port   = 80
    to_port     = 80
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }
}

resource "aws_instance" "web" {
  ami           = "ami-12345678"
  instance_type = "t3.micro"
  vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.web.id]
}
```

### Best Practices
- Use variables for AMI IDs and instance types to improve reusability
- Consider restricting CIDR blocks in production environments
- Add egress rules if specific outbound traffic control is needed
- Include tags for resource organization and cost allocation

```hcl
# main.tf
data "aws_route53_zone" "example" {
  name         = "example.com"
  private_zone = false
}

module "route53_record" {
  source = "./modules/env_tags"
  zone_id = data.aws_route53_zone.example.zone_id
  name    = "dev.example.com"
  type    = "A"
  ttl     = 300
  records = ["192.0.2.1"]
  
  environment = "dev"
  cost_center = "engineering"
}

# backend.tf
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket         = "terraform-state-bucket"
    key            = "${var.environment}/terraform.tfstate"
    region         = "us-east-1"
    encrypt        = true
    dynamodb_table = "terraform-locks"
  }
}

# modules/env_tags/main.tf
variable "zone_id" {}
variable "name" {}
variable "type" {}
variable "ttl" {}
variable "records" {}
variable "environment" {}
variable "cost_center" {}

resource "aws_route53_record" "this" {
  zone_id = var.zone_id
  name    = var.name
  type    = var.type
  ttl     = var.ttl
  records = var.records
  
  tags = {
    Environment = var.environment
    CostCenter  = var.cost_center
  }
}
```

## CI Validation Script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# ci-validate.sh
terraform plan -out=tfplan
terraform show -json tfplan > plan.json

# Check for only A record creation and tag updates
if grep -q '"change": "create"' plan.json && \
   grep -q '"aws_route53_record"' plan.json; then
  echo "✅ A record creation detected"
else
  echo "❌ Only A record creation allowed"
  exit 1
fi

# Ensure no existing records are modified
if grep -q '"change": "delete"\|"change": "update"' plan.json; then
  echo "❌ Existing record modifications not allowed"
  exit 1
fi

echo "✅ Plan validation passed"
```
